answer: Coordination Pair Tariff charges each identity a fixed fee for every first-time pairing in a multi-agent action, held until both sides confirm. An agent coordinating an opal shipment pays once per distinct counterparty. A juniper order follows the same rule, so fresh aliases create separate charges. A pearl trade illustrates the cost: each new alias pays one pairing fee per counterparty, forcing a sybil cluster needing k aliases and m counterparties to fund at least k×m fees.
